page.content:
Oasis chain from Chang'an through the Tarim to Iran and the Levant.

How Overland Silk Road connects

  • Topic: Silk Road — The oasis caravan chain is the overland half of the Silk Road.
  • Location: Chang'an — Chang'an is the classic eastern terminus of the overland road.
  • Faction: Camel caravans — Bactrian caravans were the transport of the desert legs.
  • Location: Hexi Corridor — The Hexi Corridor is the eastern bottleneck of the overland road.
  • Location: Kashgar — Kashgar is the western Tarim crossroads of the overland road.
  • Location: Samarkand — Samarkand is the Sogdian hinge of the overland road.
  • Location: Taklamakan Desert — The Taklamakan splits the Tarim legs of the overland road.
  • Character: Zhang Qian — Zhang Qian's reports made the overland west a standing Han concern.
  • Location: Palmyra — Palmyra taxed the Syrian desert approach to the Mediterranean.
  • Location: Baghdad — Abbasid Baghdad pulled overland Khurasan traffic into one capital.

What is Overland Silk Road?

The overland Silk Road ran the Hexi Corridor, split around the Taklamakan, and rejoined at Kashgar toward Samarkand and the Iranian plateau — the caravan spine Zhang Qian opened to Han knowledge.

Key threads lead to Silk Road, Chang'an, Camel caravans, Hexi Corridor, Kashgar and Samarkand.
